headline: Nigeria Issues Health Advisory For Travelers Using Addis Ababa Airport
seoTitle: Nigeria Issues Addis Ababa Transit Health Warning
metaDescription: Nigeria's foreign ministry advises citizens with medical conditions against transiting through Addis Ababa due to the airport's high altitude.
aiSummaryBullets: The Nigerian government has issued a travel warning regarding the altitude of Ethiopia’s main international airport.
The advisory specifically targets travelers with existing medical conditions who plan to transit through Addis Ababa.
Official reports indicate that several Nigerian citizens with underlying health issues have died while transiting through the city this year.
aiContextParagraph: The Nigerian Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Abuja has released a formal advisory cautioning its citizens against traveling through Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. This guidance is primarily directed at individuals who manage pre-existing medical conditions, as the capital city is situated at an elevation of 2,334 meters, or 7,657 feet, above sea level. Reports from the government attribute this warning to a series of recent incidents involving Nigerian passengers. Officials state that over the course of the current year, multiple Nigerian nationals have died while passing through the main transit hub in Addis Ababa. While reports from independent outlets vary on the specific count, with some citing six deaths and others reporting sixteen, the consistency of the government's concern regarding high-altitude health risks remains the focus of the public health communication.
whyItIsViral: This story has gained traction through reports from two independent international news outlets monitoring regional travel advisories and government communications.
